steps.u: Login works locally but on staging we get stuck in a redirect loop after the SSO callback. Chrome says too many redirects.

steps.r:
HTTP/2 302
location: https://staging.portal.example.test/auth/login
set-cookie: session=; Max-Age=0; Secure; SameSite=Strict

steps.a: The callback immediately clears the session cookie and sends the user back to login. SameSite=Strict on the session cookie would be dropped on the cross-site redirect coming back from the identity provider, but here the cookie is being set empty, which suggests the code exchange failed.

i.command: kubectl logs deploy/portal -n staging --tail=20 | grep -i callback

steps.r: WARN callback: token exchange failed: redirect_uri_mismatch (expected https://staging.portal.example.test/auth/callback, got http://staging.portal.example.test/auth/callback)

steps.a: There is the cause. The app is behind a TLS-terminating load balancer, so it thinks the request is http and builds an http redirect_uri that the identity provider rejects. Locally there is no proxy, so it matches. We need the app to trust X-Forwarded-Proto.

I have not changed anything. Two options: enable the framework's trusted-proxy setting for the load balancer's range, or hard-code the public base URL in config. I'd go with the base URL setting since it is explicit and does not depend on header trust, but it is your call.

reference.summary: Traced the staging login redirect loop to the SSO token exchange failing with redirect_uri_mismatch: behind the TLS-terminating load balancer the app built an http callback URL while the identity provider expects https. Nothing was changed; the options are trusting the forwarded protocol header or configuring a fixed public base URL.
facts: redirect loop after SSO callback on staging
app saw http behind a TLS-terminating load balancer
works locally because there is no proxy
